text:
nora: Noticed weird shift in batch distribution this morning: more 1-request batches and a p95 jump for short completion calls. Investigating.
ben: Which path? model/service? Any recent deploys?
nora: Host preproc (tokenize+normalize) on r10s. Timeline aligns with staging deploy that added utf8 normalization to preparse.
olga: Do we have perf counters? batcher metrics?
nora: Quick metrics: prior median batch size ~3.2 now 1.6 for requests <= 64 tokens. p95 latency for that cohort went 26ms -> 38ms. p99 similarly up. KV cache hitrate unchanged (~97.5%). Kernel selection logs show more assignments to small-seq kernel (seq<=64) but throughput drop overall.
ben: Interesting. If preparse now does synchronous normalize+copy per input it can add serialization jitter and collapse batching window. Grab a CPU profile and syscall trace?
sre-bot: deploy/2159 applied (preparse-utf8-normalize). Canary pool: 6 hosts.
nora: Pprof (cpu) top snippet:\n```
(pprof) top
  12.4%  host_preparse.normalize_utf8
  9.1%   host_preparse.tokenize
  7.8%   runtime.memmove
  5.0%   host_preparse.frame_assemble
  3.6%   net.grpc_writev
```
strace sample: many writes of 64-192 bytes, sometimes fragmented due to buffer-per-chunk creation.

olga: That memmove% stands out. normalize_utf8 doing copy+reencode per chunk maybe. If normalization changes length we also adjust token offsets causing tokenization extra passes?
ben: Could be double-pass: normalize then tokenize then reserialize frames. That extra work nudges request arrival jitter causing batcher to emit early singletons. Also kernel selection logs: when batch size==1 we pick pico-kernel with lower throughput.
nora: I ran a microbench: synthetic workload with 800rps of 20-60 token prompts. Three variants: (A) preparse-normalize in host (current), (B) normalize in ingress proxy (zero-copy pass-through), (C) normalize disabled. Results after steady-state run (10m):
- A: median=18ms p95=38ms avg batch size=1.6
- B: median=15ms p95=30ms avg batch size=2.9
- C: median=14ms p95=28ms avg batch size=3.1
Note: KV hits same across runs.

ben: So moving normalization to ingress reduces host memmove pressure and restores batching. Any regressions with disabling normalization? Are customers sending messy utf8?
olga: We sampled 24h of traffic: ~0.4% of requests had invalid or non-normalized sequences that previously failed downstream. Those would break if we disable normalization. But ingress can normalize and keep host cheap.
ora: I toggled dev-proxy flag proxy.normalize_utf8=true on a canary and measured: p95 host drops 38ms->31ms, batch size rises to 2.8. syscall writev count per response dropped ~2x.
ora: Another complementary fix: change host_preparse to build framed payload in a single buffer (append strategy) to avoid many small iov entries. Microbench shows further p95 drop of ~3-4ms when combined.
ben: For immediate safety do ingress normalize + proxy.coalesce_small_writes=true. Longer term: update host_preparse to zero-copy tokenize over normalized view where possible (avoid full memmove), or use SIMD-aware normalization routine to reduce memmove%.
olga: Also watch batcher.window_ms and admission. With host overhead increasing effective arrival spread, the batcher was shrinking windows. We should add a guard: if host-side median preparse>threshold, increase soft window_size to preserve throughput.
sre-bot: canary rollout: proxy.normalize_utf8=true, proxy.coalesce_small_writes=true applied to canary pool at 3112231200.
ora: After 20m of canary telemetry: p95 down to 30ms, avg batch size 2.7, kernel assignments back to normal distribution. No increase in errors.
ora: Opening two PRs: (1) ingress normalization + integration tests + canary flag, (2) host_preparse single-append-buffer rewrite with microbench and pprof. Tagging Ben & Olga for review.
ora: Action items:
- Short-term: keep ingress normalize + proxy coalesce on canary -> expand if green (Olga)
- Mid-term: host_preparse rewrite (Ben)
- Perf: add a microbench that measures batcher sensitivity to host preparse latency (Nora)
- Observability: add memmove and normalize timings to host telemetry & add kernel-selection correlation dashboard (Olga)

ben: SGTM. Also add a quick script that replays production sample through both ingress and host normalize to validate functional parity (edge cases).
ora: Thanks everyone. TL;DR: host-side utf8 normalization caused memmove-heavy overhead, which reduced avg batch size and pushed more traffic into small-kernel path. Canary ingress-normalize + proxy coalesce mitigates; host rewrite will be follow-up.
